meta.company: Panco Foods Inc. (DBA Pan's Mushroom Jerky)
meta.thesis: Pan's does not need more stores - it needs more bags sold per store, and Mushroom Mode turns H-E-B shelf space into trial.
meta.variant_angle: Pans A rev2: consistent O1 math + real visuals

business_problem: Pan's grew from ~750 to 2,500+ stores while revenue fell from $3.15M to a ~$3.0M annualized pace with losses every year: a sell-through (velocity) problem at the shelf, made worse because shoppers file it with declining plant-based meat instead of growing meat snacks.

objectives.text: Drive 1,500 attributed purchases (H-E-B coupon + online code) in 45 days, and lift units per store 25% at 6 demo stores vs. 6 control stores
Hand out 2,400 in-store samples and generate 6,000 coupon claims
Reach 1.0M Central Texas impressions and lift aided awareness by 10 points among surveyed shoppers

segments.name: Young Snack Explorers (18-29)
segments.demographic: 18-29, college students and early-career workers, Central Texas
segments.geographic: Austin, Round Rock, Georgetown, San Marcos, Waco (Texas District 5 area)
segments.psychographic: Curious about new flavors, 'better-for-you' leaning but taste-first; skeptical of products that imitate meat
segments.behavioral: Buys savory snacks weekly at H-E-B, c-stores, and campus stores; tries new snacks from creator content and friends
segments.media: TikTok and Instagram Reels daily; YouTube; group chats; low email use

segments.name: Flexitarian H-E-B Parents (30-50)
segments.demographic: 30-50, household income $60K+, parents buying lunchbox and after-school snacks
segments.geographic: Central Texas suburbs served by H-E-B
segments.psychographic: Wants cleaner snacks with no allergens to worry about; open to plant-based but not willing to pay for disappointment
segments.behavioral: Weekly H-E-B shopper; uses the H-E-B app and digital coupons; buys meat snacks for kids
segments.media: Facebook, Instagram, H-E-B app, email newsletters

methods.recruitment: SEC filing, GFI/SPINS, Circana via trade press, company pages

programs.name: Mushroom Mode Demo Days
programs.mechanic: 12 weekend demo shifts at 6 Central Texas H-E-B test stores; sample cups beside the jerky set; QR to the '$2 off 2 bags' coupon. 6 matched control stores get the coupon but no demos or clip strip, isolating the in-store effect.

programs.name: The Aisle Switch
programs.mechanic: Pitched to H-E-B's snack buyer in October-November: clip strip inside the meat-snack set at 6 test stores, shelf talker, and '$2 off 2 bags' app coupon at all ~40 Central Texas stores carrying Pan's. Fallback if declined: demos + Pan's own printable coupon.

programs.name: Mushroom Mode Taste-Off
programs.mechanic: 3 Texas food creators run blind taste-offs: Pan's vs. their favorite beef jerky. Link goes to a store finder + coupon, or the online Texas Starter Pack with code MUSHROOMMODE. #ad disclosure on every post.

programs.name: Founder's Table
programs.mechanic: Michael Pan's Malaysia recipe-to-Shark Tank story in 3 short videos and 3 emails/SMS to the existing list, each ending with the store finder and the Texas Starter Pack code.

assumptions.text: Blended net revenue per purchase $19: 50% retail coupon purchases at $6 (2 bags x ~$4 wholesale minus $2 coupon) + 50% online Texas Starter Packs at $32 (5 bags at $8 minus 20% code); confirm wholesale price with company

Blended gross margin 53%: retail $2.64 GP on $6 using $1.67/bag cost [S3]; online $17.65 GP on $32 after 5 x $1.67 and ~$6 shipping/packing. Cross-check: SEC figures imply 30-57% margins FY22-FY24 [S1]
H-E-B store-level baseline velocity unknown; measured week 0 via shelf audit + company sell-through data
Impressions 1.0M = ~670K paid at ~$6 CPM ($4,000) + ~330K creator views (3 creators); 1.5% click rate; 10% click-to-purchase (validate week 1). In-store exposure not counted in the funnel
Pan's and H-E-B would approve in-store demos and a digital coupon (proposed, not confirmed)
Texas food micro-creators (10K-80K followers): ~$750 per video incl. product
In-store demo shift ~$200 (4-hr demo staff via sampling agency + product for ~200 samples)
$2 off 2 bags manufacturer coupon; its cost is netted out of revenue per purchase (A1), not a separate line
Production (shelf talkers, clip strips, sample cups, design) ~$700 via local print shop quotes
Email/SMS + landing page tools ~$300 for the campaign window
Repeat: 30% of campaign buyers buy once more within 90 days at the same blended gross profit (~$10.15); confirm with company data
Velocity baseline: FY24 revenue $2.78M over 11 months / 2,500 stores / ~$4 wholesale = at most ~6 bags per store per week (upper bound; includes online sales)
Demo-day purchases (~20% of 2,400 sampled shoppers = ~480) are upside not counted in the funnel
~40 Central Texas H-E-B stores carry Pan's (estimate; confirm with the store locator at mushroomjerky.com)
Texas Starter Pack: 5-bag online bundle at $40 with 20% off code MUSHROOMMODE; site offers free shipping over $30

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Thesis: Pan's does not need more stores - it needs more bags sold per store [S1].
Problem: stores grew from ~750 to 2,500+ while revenue fell from $3.15M (FY22) - at most ~6 bags per store per week [S1][S2][S4][A14].
Opportunity: meat snacks +11.3% to $6.4B while plant-based meat fell 10% - Pan's sits in the wrong mental aisle [S6][S7].
Solution: 'Switch to Mushroom Mode' puts Pan's in the jerky shopper's decision at Central Texas H-E-B stores and online [O1].
45-day goal: 1,500 attributed purchases and +25% units per store at demo stores vs. control [O1].

visual.desc: Four boxes: Problem / Business opportunity / Solution / 45-day goal

slides.notes: Open with the paradox: Pan's went from about 750 stores to 2,500, yet revenue fell. The problem is not distribution - it is what happens at the shelf.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Shiitake mushroom jerky from a decades-old Pan family recipe found in Malaysia; chewy, savory, umami [S2].
Vegan, gluten-free, Kosher, no allergens to declare; the brand says it 'isn't trying to completely imitate beef' [S5].
Shelf price $7.99-$8.99 per 2.2 oz bag; cost to make about $1.67 per bag at launch [S3].
Four core flavors; sold online, on Amazon, and in grocery including H-E-B in Texas [S2][S10].

visual.desc: Flat-lay of four flavor bags with a torn-open bag showing the jerky texture

slides.notes: Stress the brand's own words: it is not trying to be beef. That line becomes our whole positioning.

slides.title: The Company & Its Position
bullets: Founded by engineer Michael Pan; launched 2018; Mark Cuban invested $300K for 18% on Shark Tank (2020) [S3][S4].
Revenue $3.15M (FY22) -> $2.88M (FY23) -> $2.78M (11 months FY24); net loss every year [S1].
Competitors, 52 weeks to Aug 2025: Jack Link's $898M (-5.8%), Chomps $797M (+61.5%), Old Trapper +4% [S8].
Position: savory like jerky and honest that it is not beef - unlike plant-based meat built to imitate meat [S5][S6].

visual.desc: Left: revenue FY22-FY24 falling vs. store count rising. Right: positioning map (x = meat-based to plant-based, y = imitates meat to honest snack) with Jack Link's, Chomps, Old Trapper, plant-based meat brands, and Pan's alone in the 'plant-based + honest snack' quadrant

slides.notes: This is our most important slide for credibility: every number comes from the company's own SEC filing.

slides.title: Campaign Objectives
bullets: O1 (primary): 1,500 attributed purchases (750 H-E-B coupon + 750 online) and +25% units per store at 6 demo stores vs. 6 control [O1].
Baseline: at most ~6 bags per store per week today [A14].
O2 (consideration): 2,400 in-store samples and 6,000 coupon claims [O2].
O3 (awareness): 1.0M Central Texas impressions and +10 points aided awareness [O3].

visual.desc: O1-O3 with funnel stage, metric, target, and test-vs-control design

slides.notes: One primary objective - bags sold - measured against control stores, so the client sees lift, not noise.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1 Young Snack Explorers, 18-29: Central Texas college students and young workers who buy snacks weekly and try new ones from TikTok and friends; skeptical of fake meat [S8][S11].
P2 Flexitarian H-E-B Parents, 30-50: weekly H-E-B shoppers using app coupons; want snacks with no allergens to worry about [S5][S9].
Both share one need: a savory snack that is honest about what it is - the reason Pan's says it is not imitating beef [S5].
Market: 6 in 10 US households already buy plant-based foods [S11].

visual.desc: Two persona cards (P1, P2) with photo, demographics, psychographics, and media habits

slides.notes: Interactive moment: show the two persona cards printed side by side.

slides.title: Research Method & Results
bullets: Secondary (complete): SEC filing, GFI/SPINS, Circana via trade press, company pages - 11 sources [S1][S6][S7][S8].
Key results: revenue down while stores up [S1][S2]; meat snacks +11.3% [S7]; plant-based meat -10% [S6]; jerky flat while meat sticks surge [S8].
Primary (in field): 10-question survey of Central Texas snack buyers, 3-5 shopper interviews with taste test, and an H-E-B shelf audit at 3 stores.
Influences: protein snacking boom (social), plant-based fatigue (cultural), food inflation (economic), app coupons (technological) [S6][S7][S9].

visual.desc: Methods table (4 methods, n, dates, status) + bar chart of category growth: meat snacks +11.3%, plant-based meat -10%

slides.notes: Name the methods and sample sizes out loud. When the survey closes, the bar chart gets our own results.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: Finding: store count up, revenue down [S1][S2] -> therefore we fund trial at the shelf (Demo Days), not more distribution.
Finding: meat snacks +11.3%, plant-based meat -10% [S6][S7] -> therefore Pan's is placed and messaged next to jerky, not with fake meat (Aisle Switch).
Finding: brand says it is not imitating beef [S5] -> therefore creators run honest taste-offs instead of 'tastes just like beef' claims.
Finding: losses every year [S1] -> therefore every dollar is trackable (coupons, QR, test vs. control).

visual.desc: Four finding -> therefore rows with source tags

slides.notes: Every decision traces to evidence. Point at the arrows, not the text.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Big idea: Mushroom Mode - not fake meat, a savory snack you switch into. Message: 'Love jerky? Switch to Mushroom Mode.'
Positioning: for Texas snackers who want something savory and honest, Pan's is the jerky made from shiitake that does not pretend to be beef [S5].
IMC mix: Paid (geo social) + Earned (Shark Tank founder story) + Shared (#MushroomMode duets) + Owned (email/SMS, shelf talkers).
Push-pull: H-E-B gets a measurable velocity test (push); shoppers get samples and a coupon (pull) [O1][O2].

visual.desc: Key visual: split frame - beef jerky aisle on left, Pan's bag glowing on right, 'Switch to Mushroom Mode' lockup

slides.notes: Point to the positioning statement. A competitor that imitates meat cannot say this line - that is what makes it ownable.

slides.title: Program 1: Mushroom Mode Demo Days
bullets: Mushroom Mode in person: 12 weekend demo shifts at 6 Central Texas H-E-B test stores; 6 control stores get the coupon only [O1][O2].
Mechanic: sample cups at the jerky set; QR code to '$2 off 2 bags'; 200 samples per shift = 2,400 total [A7][A8].
Why: at ~6 bags per store per week, shoppers are walking past - sampling turns curiosity into trial [A14].
Measured: QR scans per store and units per store vs. control stores [O1].

visual.desc: Demo table mockup: orange tablecloth, 'Switch to Mushroom Mode' banner, sample cups, QR sign

slides.notes: Interactive moment: hand the judge the printed shelf talker and sample-cup sleeve.

slides.title: Program 2: The Aisle Switch
bullets: Mushroom Mode on the shelf: proposed clip strip inside the H-E-B meat-snack set at 6 test stores [O1].
Sell-in: pitched to H-E-B's snack buyer in October-November as a 6-week velocity test; fallback is demos + Pan's printable coupon.
App coupon at all ~40 Central Texas stores carrying Pan's: 'Love jerky? Switch to Mushroom Mode. $2 off 2 bags.' [A8][A16][O2]
Why: meat snacks are growing 11.3% - Pan's should be where those shoppers already stand [S7].

visual.desc: Shelf mockup: Pan's clip strip hanging between Jack Link's and Chomps, orange shelf talker with QR

slides.notes: This is a proposal to H-E-B's buyer, framed as a 6-week velocity test with control stores; the fallback keeps the campaign alive if they say no.

slides.title: Program 3: Taste-Off + Founder's Table
bullets: Mushroom Mode online: 3 Texas food creators run blind Pan's vs. beef jerky taste-offs; fans duet with #MushroomMode [O1][O3].
Every video links to the store finder + coupon or the online Texas Starter Pack (code MUSHROOMMODE) with #ad disclosure [A17].
Founder's Table: Michael Pan tells the Malaysia recipe-to-Shark Tank story in 3 videos and 3 emails/SMS [S2][S3].
Named decision-maker: Mark Cuban's investment is the credibility hook for the H-E-B pitch [S4].

slides.title: Proposed Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $10,000: paid social $4,000 [A4]; creators 3 x $750 = $2,250 [A6]; demos 12 x $200 = $2,400 [A7]; production $700 [A9]; tools $300 [A10]; contingency $350 [A11].
Funnel: 1.0M impressions x 1.5% x 10% = 1,500 purchases; half H-E-B coupon ($6 net), half online packs ($32) = $19 avg, $28.5K [A1][A4].
Gross profit at 53% = $15.1K; profit ROI 51%; ROAS 4.6x on $6.25K ad spend [A2].
Conservative (50%): 750 purchases, ROI -24%; with 30% repeat in 90 days it reaches about break-even [A13].
Upside not counted: ~480 demo-day purchases [A15].

visual.desc: Itemized budget table + funnel math + base vs. conservative case

slides.notes: Lead with honesty: in-window it breaks even; the return comes from repeat buyers and from keeping shelf space. Then show the test-vs-control design that proves it.

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1: attributed purchases; baseline 0; target 1,500; H-E-B coupon + Shopify code reports; weekly [O1].
O1: units per store per week, demo vs. control; baseline <= ~6 [A14]; target +25%; retailer data; weekly [O1].
O2: samples and claims; baseline 0; target 2,400 and 6,000; tally sheets + coupon platform; weekly [O2].
O3: 1.0M impressions; aided awareness via pre/post survey of 150 shoppers; target +10 pts [O3].
Trigger: under 20 QR scans per shift by week 3, move demos to the top 3 stores; creator click rate under 1%, shift spend to Meta [A4].

visual.desc: KPI table: objective -> KPI -> baseline -> target -> tool -> cadence

slides.notes: Test vs. control is what a CPG buyer wants: proof the lift came from the campaign.

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Thesis: Pan's does not need more stores - it needs more bags sold per store. Mushroom Mode turns H-E-B shelf space into trial [O1].
Projected: 1,500 purchases and $15.1K gross profit on $10K (51% ROI), plus a test-vs-control result Pan's can take to every retailer [A1][O1].
Mission: a family recipe from Malaysia, honest about what it is - kept on Texas shelves because Texans tried it [S2][S5].
Next: if test stores beat control by 25%, roll Mushroom Mode to more H-E-B stores [O1].
